## Overview

`meteogal2fdata` reads daily meteorological observations from the MeteoGalicia
station network as ordinary R `data.frame` objects. The workflow is designed to
keep the original measurements (including missing values) and to convert them
to functional objects with `fda.usc` only when needed. Daily records retain
February 29; conversion to annual curves later uses a common 365-day grid.

The package uses **base R** for date handling and data manipulation.
`jsonlite` is required for native daily JSON online requests. `meteospain`
is used for station inventory and is an optional legacy backend; `sf`
reads original spatial `.rda` archives. Data source:
MeteoGalicia, Xunta de Galicia.

## An offline example

The package includes `meteogal_small.csv`, a six-day extract for station 10157
(Coruña-Torre de Hércules, January 1-6, 2024). The values reproduce the
historical data checked during package development; this **small fixture is
not a complete annual series**.

```{r local-example}
library(meteogal2fdata)
f <- system.file("extdata", "meteogal_small.csv", package = "meteogal2fdata")
mg <- meteogal2df(data_dir = f, vars = c("temp_mean", "prec"))
head(mg[, c("fecha", "station_id", "temp_mean", "prec")])
str(mg[, c("fecha", "temp_mean", "prec")])
```

Station identifiers are strings, so identifiers containing leading zeros are
not changed. The `fecha` column has class `Date`. Missing values remain `NA`.

## Inventory

The online inventory lists the stations currently returned by the service.
It does not necessarily include every station that has ever operated.

```{r online-inventory, eval=FALSE}
inv <- meteogal2inventory(file = "meteogal_inventory.rds")
head(inv)
```

An inventory for local archives can be reconstructed without accessing the
service. `first_date` and `last_date` describe coverage in the available
files, not official opening and closure dates.

```{r historical-inventory, eval=FALSE}
inv_old <- meteogal2inventory(data_dir = "../meteogalicia/data")
head(inv_old)
```

## Daily downloads and safe resumption

Online requests use the native MeteoGalicia daily JSON endpoint. Large date ranges are
split into natural calendar months by default; short testing intervals are
recommended before downloading long historical series.

```{r online-data, eval=FALSE}
# Most recent 30 days for one station
recent <- meteogal2df(station_ids = "10157", vars = c("temp_mean", "prec"))

# Store monthly downloads in per-station, per-year .rds files
log <- meteogal2download("2024-01-01", "2024-12-31",
                          station_ids = "10157", out_dir = "meteogal_daily")
print(log)
```

Successful windows are cached under `meteogal_daily/_tmp_qc/`. If a window fails,
its corresponding final station-year output is not written. Restarting the same
request reuses successful windows unless `overwrite = TRUE`.

## Reading historical downloads

The reader accepts the original `meteogalicia_YYYY.rda` files as well as
station-year `.rds` archives written by `meteogal2download()`.

```{r historical-read, eval=FALSE}
mg_2024 <- meteogal2df(
  data_dir = "../meteogalicia/data/meteogalicia_2024.rda",
  station_ids = "10157", vars = c("temp_mean", "prec"))
stopifnot(nrow(mg_2024) == 366L)  # 2024 is a leap year
```

For a larger **real** bundled example, run `data-raw/build-example.R` once
from the package root. It uses the existing 2023/2024 `.rda` archives,
selects two adequately observed stations, and writes
`inst/extdata/meteogal_example.csv` plus a sample-station inventory.
It does not contact the API.

```{r generated-example}
full <- system.file("extdata", "meteogal_example.csv", package = "meteogal2fdata")
if (nzchar(full)) {
  extended <- meteogal2df(data_dir = full, vars = c("temp_mean", "prec"))
  print(table(extended$station_id, format(extended$fecha, "%Y")))
} else {
  cat("Optional two-station sample not yet generated; run data-raw/build-example.R.\n")
}
```

## Data provenance

Data are provided by MeteoGalicia (Xunta de Galicia). Record download dates,
selected stations, measurement units and the source period in reproducible
applications. Unobserved dates should never be confused with observations
whose measurement value is missing.

## Validation status of individual measurements

MeteoGalicia's daily JSON defines validation code `lnCodigoValidacion` for
each recorded parameter: 0 = not validated, 1 = valid original, 2 = suspect,
3 = erroneous, 5 = valid interpolated, 9 = not recorded. New downloads
preserve these codes as `qc_temp_mean`, `qc_prec`, and so on. The numeric
measurement columns are stored without quality filtering.

```{r qc-offline, eval=TRUE}
# Small synthetic example: these codes reproduce the official definitions.
qc_example <- data.frame(fecha = as.Date(c("2024-01-01", "2024-01-02")),
                         station_id = "10157", temp_mean = c(10, 12),
                         qc_temp_mean = c(1L, 2L))
fd <- meteogal2fdata(df = qc_example, var = "temp_mean", quality = 1)
fd$data[1, 1:2]  # second value masked to NA
```

When reading locally saved files, `meteogal2df(quality = c(1, 5))` is the
default, and `quality = 1` admits only original observations. Rejected values
are `NA`, **but quality columns are never dropped**. `quality = NULL`
allows suspect and unvalidated measurements but never codes 3 or 9.

The daily service supports selecting `idEst`, `idParam`, `dataIni` and `dataFin`,
but does not document a server-side filter for the validation code.
Therefore `meteogal2download(vars=...)` selects variables on the server,
while the quality criterion is applied locally without losing original data.
The web form has documented query-volume restrictions, which are **not**
a documented JSON API quota.

Official source documents:

- <https://www.meteogalicia.gal/datosred/infoweb/meteo/docs/rss/JSON_EstacionsDiarios_es.pdf>
- <https://www.meteogalicia.gal/datosred/infoweb/meteo/docs/informes/datos_es.pdf>
